newsitem.title: BELGIUM: SGB sold 24 pct Union Miniere stake.
newsitem.headline: SGB sold 24 pct Union Miniere stake.

text.p: Belgian holding company Societe Generale de Belgique SA (SGB) said on Wednesday it sold a 24 percent stake in Belgian non-ferrous metals group Union Miniere SA (UM) to a banking syndicate.
The syndicate will place the shares with Belgian and international institutional investors, SGB said in a statement.
The sale raised about 20 billion francs ($550.8 million). SGB added it would book a capital gain of about 12 billion francs on the operation.
SGB would hold on to 25 percent of UM's capital and would remain the leading shareholder.
SGB said that revenue from the stake sale would wipe out most of the debt taken on to finance the acquisition of a minority stake in Belgian utility holding company Tractebel SA in 1996.

An SGB spokesman told Reuters that following the sale, and if investors exchanged SGB bonds convertible into Arbed shares in December for an amount of two billion francs, SGB's debt would fall to zero at the end of 1997. Others too cited Merrill Lynch as a large seller of Union Miniere. ($ = 36.31 Belgian Francs)
